summary: Intermittent dashboard metric drop and missing trace-links during ingestion backoff window
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that several dashboard panels for hourly usage and SLA cards temporarily drop to 0 or show large negative spikes during short ingestion backoff periods. Concurrently, trace links from those dashboard rows to the trace viewer are missing for the same time slices.
impact: Multiple NimbusHealth engineering dashboards spiked alerts (sev2) and lost trace context for a 2-6 minute window during scheduled traffic ripples. Affects visibility for on-call and automated alerting for core usage-based SLAs. No model inference correctness impact reported.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer force a connector retry/backoff on their ingest stream (simulated by toggling throttling at the edge or by temporarily increasing request latency).
2) Send a 5-minute burst of synthetic API traffic at normal rates, then induce a 2-4 minute backoff where the connector retries with exponential backoff.
3) Open NimbusHealth org dashboard > SLA card (last 1h) and hourly usage panel aligned to us-west-2.
4) Observe the panel: during the backoff window the usage drops to 0 and SLA card shows a spike (false alert).
5) Click a row in the affected time bucket and verify that the trace link opens the trace viewer; observed: link is absent or 404s for window timestamps.
observed_logs: ingest-pipeline: WARN connector-retry: backoff=3s next_attempt=2026-03-10T14:03:12Z batch_size=64
ingest-pipeline: INFO ingest-rollup: 0 events committed for shard=s3-ingest-03 window=2026-03-10T14:00:00Z - 2026-03-10T14:05:00Z
trace-linker: ERROR link-attach: trace-anchor-missing for event_id=evt_7f3a2, org=nimbushealth, timestamp=2026-03-10T14:02:45Z
console-ui: ERROR dashboard-render: timeseries-alignment-mismatch bucket=2026-03-10T14:00:00Z cause=ingest-eviction
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: connector backoff causes temporary ingestion window to be marked as empty and rollup job emits zero-count buckets; downstream trace-linker expects event anchors that are pruned during aggressive compaction/eviction.
Checked Kinesis/Kafka metrics: transient consumer lag spike coincident with reported window (consumer-lag peaked ~3.4s).
Rollup logs show a zero-commit for the affected shard window; confirmed by rollup-runner logs on ingest-03 host.

Trace linker errors show missing event anchors: anchor TTL policy evicted keys older than 2 minutes when consumer lag > threshold, which removed anchor entries before rollup reconciler attempted to attach traces.
Reproduced in staging by setting intentional consumer lag; confirmed both dashboard zeroing and missing trace-links within 2-6 minute lag windows.
Related config: anchor-ttl currently set to 120s, rollup-grace-window configured to 180s — race condition when backoff causes consumer lag > TTL.
comments: Aisha Ramaswamy (Support): Logged after customer call. Customer saw alerts trigger and oncall escalated. Asked SRE to investigate retention/ttl mismatch.

Jonah Park (SRE): Reproduced in staging. I've opened a short-term mitigation: increase anchor-ttl to 300s for NimbusHealth org; applied via feature-flag rollout. Monitoring for a second customer-impact window.
Customer (NimbusHealth - ops): Confirmed dashboards stopped firing false alerts after temporary fix. Can we get permanent fix ETA?

Jonah Park (SRE): Permanent fix requires changing rollup reconciliation to not assume anchors exist and to fallback to event index lookups. Will propose change in PR and schedule canary. ETA 3 business days for PR + canary, 7 days for full rollout.
Support (Aisha): Added linked ticket to billing if any alert-driven incident incurs cost; customer does not request credits at this time.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: increased anchor-ttl from 120s to 300s for NimbusHealth org via feature flag to avoid eviction during consumer lag spikes. Permanent fix: implement rollup reconciler fallback to event-index lookup when anchor missing; code change approved as github.com/redwood-inference/trace-linker/pull/2531 and scheduled for canary on 2026-03-15. Close post-canary and customer confirmation.
